data.title: Jason Calacanis Calls Bitcoin Boring as Michael Saylor Defends Its Long-Term Value
data.description:
On September 19, venture capitalist Jason Calacanis posted a critical message about Bitcoin after it moved back above $80,000, comparing it to CDs in the Spotify era and DVDs in the Netflix era. According to ChainCatcher, he said Bitcoin is weak for trading and smart contracts, offers a poor user experience, and no longer captures the public imagination.

Calacanis added that if Bitcoin were going to achieve mass adoption and major use cases, it would have done so already. He also said people now expect Bitcoin to remain stable, described it as no longer a fast path to wealth, and mocked its advocates as having shifted from pirates to suit-wearing figures sharing awkward memes.

MicroStrategy co-founder Michael Saylor responded that Bitcoin has grown into a $1.6 trillion success and the world’s most valuable digital asset. He said digital capital is the killer app and that preserving wealth across generations is a bigger ambition than pleasing dinner guests. Saylor also said the orange tie will stay on.

data.title: XRP Whale Activity Rises as Large Holders Buy 1.54 Billion Tokens in 96 Hours
data.description: XRP network whale activity increased over the past 96 hours, with large holders appearing to have accumulated about 1.54 billion XRP worth roughly $2 billion. According to Odaily, the figures were tracked by Ali Charts.

data.title: Linera and Switchboard Announce Closures as RootData’s Dead Crypto Projects List Tops 260
data.description:
Linera and Switchboard announced closures on September 18 and September 19, respectively, as RootData’s 2026 list of dead crypto projects passed 260 entries. According to NS3.AI, Linera said it stopped operations after a Sonar sale drew close to $900,000, falling short of its $1.5 million USDC minimum target.

Switchboard said remaining support will end on September 25, 2026. The project directed developers to alternative providers including Pyth and RedStone, and cited recent exploits, cheaper AI tools, slower new-chain launches and reduced budgets as factors behind the decision.

data.title: Robinhood Chain Fee Revenue Falls 97% From Peak as Meme Coin Trading Holds Volume
data.description: Robinhood Chain fee revenue has fallen 97% from its peak, according to CoinDesk. According to ChainCatcher, on-chain trading volume has not seen a major outflow and has remained at the tens of millions level, supported by lingering meme coin trading activity.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | ECB Should Stay Vigilant, Not Rush, Stournaras Says
data.description:
European Central Bank Governing Council member Yannis Stournaras said the ECB must be mindful of upside inflation risks but should not act hastily, according to Bloomberg.

He said the central bank should remain vigilant.

data.title: US to Return $2.5 Million Seized From Property Linked to Ex-Gambian Dictator
data.description: The US will transfer $2.5 million recovered from a Maryland property tied to former Gambian dictator Yahya Jammeh to compensate eligible victims of his more than 22-year rule, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Jon Gray Says India’s Growth Story Is Drawing Global Investors
data.description:
Blackstone Chief Operating Officer Jon Gray said India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are attracting global investors, according to Bloomberg.

He also said millions of young people graduate each year while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. Indian states are competing for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors.

data.title: Bastion Receives Preliminary OCC Approval for U.S. Trust Bank Charter
data.description: Bastion said the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval for a U.S. trust bank charter. According to NS3.AI, the proposed bank would offer stablecoin custody, wallets, payment infrastructure, and white-label issuance, but it would not be allowed to accept deposits or make loans.

data.title: Supertanker Shortage Threatens Long-Haul Oil Trade
data.description: Rising costs to ship oil globally are making some long-distance crude trades uneconomical, threatening to disrupt flows as fuel markets remain tight, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Miller Cole Says Bitcoin-Gold Ratio Reclaimed 50-Week Average
data.description:
Miller Cole, research and content analyst at Bitcoin treasury company The Smarter Web Company, said on X that 1 bitcoin is now worth about 18.55 ounces of gold, up from about 15.3 ounces a month ago. According to ChainCatcher, he said Friday's bitcoin price move pushed the BTC/XAU ratio back above its 50-week simple moving average, which he described as a bullish signal.

Cole added that he expects the BTC/XAU ratio to reach a new high during the current cycle over the next few years.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Pakistan Police Headquarters Attack Kills 31
data.description:
A militant attack on a police headquarters in northwestern Pakistan killed at least 31 people, officials said, according to Bloomberg.

The violence came in the region bordering Afghanistan as clashes between security forces and militants escalate.

data.title: Volkswagen Reportedly Plans to Cut About 4,100 More Jobs at Porsche
data.description:
Volkswagen is reportedly planning to cut about 4,100 jobs at Porsche as part of a broader turnaround effort after issuing a profit warning tied to problems at its sports-car subsidiary. According to Sina Finance, a document recording a recent agreement reached by Volkswagen's supervisory board said the group plans to reduce Porsche's workforce by about 4,100 employees to address an operating cost gap of about 700 million euros, or about $803.8 million.

The report said the layoffs would be carried out outside existing agreements. In July, Porsche management and labor representatives agreed to cut an additional 5,000 jobs on top of an earlier plan to eliminate 4,000 positions, which would bring total cuts to about one-fifth of the company's workforce by 2035.

data.title: FedEx Taps Polish Billionaire Rafal Brzoska for Europe Push
data.description:
FedEx is counting on Polish billionaire Rafal Brzoska to help crack European markets, according to Bloomberg.

Brzoska built InPost into a parcel company operating in nine countries, though the path was not always smooth.

data.title: Brazil Central Bank to Bar Stablecoins in Regulated FX Settlement From Oct. 1
data.description: Brazil's central bank will prohibit virtual assets, including stablecoins, from being used to settle the leg between regulated foreign-exchange providers and overseas counterparties from Oct. 1 under Resolution 561. According to NS3.AI, individual international transfers using virtual assets will still be allowed, but the restriction could add FX, banking, and correspondent costs to aggregated payment flows. Brazil's tax authority recorded R$1.13 trillion in declared stablecoin transactions from August 2019 through December 2025.

data.title: Paramount, States May Settle Warner Bros. Deal Fight As Soon As This Weekend
data.description: According to CNBC, Paramount and states seeking to block its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. could reach a settlement as soon as this weekend, with independent content monitoring of CNN and a commitment on the number of theatrical releases among the terms under discussion. Paramount shares rose nearly 7% after markets closed, while Warner Bros. Discovery shares gained 8.4% in after-market trading. The case brought by California and 11 other states is one of the final hurdles to Paramount's bid to become a larger rival to Netflix and Walt Disney, and a settlement this week could help Paramount avoid paying millions of dollars in fees to Warner Bros. shareholders. Paramount is on the hook for a $7 million-a-day ticking fee after September 30 until the deal closes, and CEO David Ellison has previously said the combined film studios would release 30 movies a year.

data.title: USDC Treasury Mints 250 Million USDC on Solana
data.description: USDC Treasury minted 250 million USDC on the Solana blockchain at 18:36 (UTC+8). According to Odaily, the new issuance was recorded on-chain.

data.title: South Korean Police Identify 26 Polymarket Users in Illegal Gambling Probe
data.description:
South Korea’s Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province Police Agency cyber investigation unit identified 26 Polymarket users after analyzing public blockchain transaction records and on-chain open-source intelligence, and filed cases on suspicion of illegal gambling. According to Odaily, 18 of them have been referred to prosecutors, with total bets reaching $12.7 million and the largest single-user wager at $4.1 million.

Police began a preliminary investigation in March and filed cases against those involved in May. The Korea Communications Standards Commission ordered Polymarket blocked on August 18, but the transactions under investigation took place while the platform was still accessible. Police are pursuing the case under Article 246 of South Korea’s Criminal Act.

data.title: Glassnode Says Bitcoin Buyers Are Strong Enough to Absorb Profit-Taking
data.description: Glassnode said current market buying demand is strong enough for Bitcoin holders to sell at a profit without immediately triggering a price pullback. According to Odaily, the firm said an entity-adjusted SOPR staying above 1 is typically a feature of a bull market, while a drop below 1 could indicate weakening demand.

data.title: MultiversX Investigates Potential Issue Detected on Mainnet
data.description: MultiversX said on X that its team is investigating a potential issue detected on the mainnet, with its top priority being user protection and keeping the network secure and reliable. According to Odaily, MultiversX said it will provide another update within the next 12 hours or once it reaches a clear conclusion.

data.title: MultiversX Investigates Potential Issue Detected on Mainnet
data.description:
MultiversX said it is investigating a potential issue detected on its mainnet. According to ChainCatcher, the team said its top priority remains protecting users and ensuring the network continues to operate securely and reliably.

MultiversX said it will provide further updates within the next 12 hours or once it reaches a clear conclusion.
